To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the accuracy of collaborative filtering recommender system predictions depends strongly on the type of user task, and that (ii) the choice of prediction accuracy metric has little effect on the ranking of algorithms, but can have a strong effect on the ranking within each algorithm.

(1) the accuracy of a recommender system depends on the task, (2) there are at least three distinct types of tasks, (3) the best metric depends on the task and (4) there is a single metric that is good for all three tasks.

the evaluation of collaborative filtering recommender system performance is strongly dependent on: (1) whether the system is used for a top-N recommendation task or a rating prediction task; (2) whether the system uses a memory-based or model-based algorithm; and (3) whether the system makes predictions on held-out test users or on the same users whose data was used to build the model.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a wide range of metrics, but that the best metric for a given application depends on what is being optimized for and what the domain is.
the best evaluation strategy is to use the most relevant user task and to use a metric from the same equivalence class as that used in prior work.
the best metric is the one that best matches the evaluation goals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evaluation of collaborative filtering recommender algorithms is a difficult and subtle problem.
, in our domain, the accuracy of the recommendation system is not affected by the evaluation metric chosen, as long as it is a member of the same equivalency class.

the accuracy metric used to evaluate a recommender system is not nearly as important as the user task being evaluated, the dataset used, the way in which the system is deployed, and the way in which users interact with the system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given dataset, there is a limited set of metrics that should be used for evaluating recommender systems.
there is no one best accuracy metric for all recommender systems.
there are many ways to evaluate recommender systems and no one way to do it.
